answer: Before an agent can attest, it must lock a slashable bond in the protocol vault for at least one full epoch. Registrations that share a hardware or network locus collapse to a single knoll, so only one bond is recognized. If coordinated posting is proven, every linked bond is slashed. An attacker who wants to drive a gale of votes must therefore buy, lock, and risk forfeiting a distinct bond for every extra name, making the cost of each fake identity explicit and linear.
